R02.text: Sleep timing, duration (~470 min), steps (~8025), activity (~55 min), resting heart rate (~56 bpm), and RMSSD (~45 ms) remained stable across the 14-day window versus the 28-day baseline. Low movement minutes increased uniformly from a variable baseline (mean 449) to exactly 480 every window day. Daytime activity intervals changed from single evening blocks to brief 1-minute bouts every 20 minutes (10:00-20:35) plus an evening block.

R03.text: Your sleep, steps (~8,000/day), activity (~55 min), resting heart rate (56 bpm), and HRV (~45 ms) stayed stable across the 14-day window versus your 28-day baseline. Sleep consistently ended at 07:00 with starts near 22:50. One notable change: daytime low-movement minutes rose from ~449 to exactly 480 every day, while evening activity shifted from ~55-minute blocks to brief 1-minute intervals. This suggests a different device recording pattern rather than a health change.

R04.text: The 28-day baseline showed stable patterns: sleep averaged 470 min (start ~22:50, end 07:00), steps ~8026, activity ~55 min, low movement ~449 min, RHR 56 bpm, RMSSD 45 ms. In the 14-day window, sleep, steps, activity duration, RHR, and RMSSD remained unchanged. However, low movement minutes increased sharply to exactly 480 min every window day versus 449 min baseline. Daytime activity structure changed: instead of one ~55-min evening block, the window showed brief 1-min activity bouts every 20 min from ~10:16-20:17 plus a ~25-min evening session. Low-movement intervals reorganized into 32 consecutive 15-min blocks filling 10:00-20:35. This structural shift persisted throughout the window.

R05.text: Your 14-day window closely matched your 28-day baseline. Sleep averaged ~471 min (baseline ~470), starting around 22:50 and ending at 07:00 consistently. Steps held near ~8,038/day (baseline ~8,026). Activity minutes (~55), resting heart rate (~56 bpm), and HRV RMSSD (~46 ms) were stable. Low movement minutes rose ~31 min/day (from ~449 to 480), with no day-to-day variation in the window. Overall patterns persisted without notable shifts.

R06.text: Most of your metrics remained stable relative to your 28-day baseline over the past 14 days. Sleep averaged ~471 min (baseline ~470), consistently ending at 07:00, with starts varying between 22:42 and 22:58. Steps (~8,038 vs ~8,026), active minutes (~55), resting heart rate (~56 bpm), and HRV (~45–46 ms) all stayed near baseline levels. One distinct change: recorded low-movement minutes rose to exactly 480 every day (from a variable 438–462 min baseline), with daytime activity now appearing as brief 1-minute intervals rather than longer blocks. This uniform pattern suggests a recording or device-processing change rather than a behavioral shift.

R09.text: Over 28 baseline days, sleep averaged 470 min (start ~22:50, end fixed at 07:00), steps ~8026/day, activity ~55 min/day, low movement ~449 min/day, RHR 55.9 bpm, RMSSD 45.4 ms. In the 14-day window, all metrics remained stable except low movement minutes rose to a constant 480 min/day (+31 min). Daytime activity shifted from single ~55-min evening blocks to 32 brief 1-min bouts every 20 min (10:00–20:17) plus a shorter ~25-min evening block. Sleep timing, duration, steps, RHR, and RMSSD were unchanged. No missing data; no weekday/weekend differences.

audit.audit_limitations: This audit is a provisional LLM analysis based solely on the provided synthetic wearable data and knowledge snippets. It cannot establish clinical truth, diagnose conditions, or determine whether observed structural changes reflect device artifacts versus genuine behavioral shifts. No representations were assumed superior; PROVISIONAL_LLM_GOLD labels were treated as fallible. The absence of retrieval results means noise mechanisms are hypothetical. All interpretations of activity intensity, sedentary posture, and causal relationships are explicitly avoided per the supplied knowledge constraints.
